question: Non-stick pans are coated with __________.
solution:
The correct answer is **polytetrafluoroethylene** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Non-stick frying pans are coated with Teflon.**

 
 
• Nonstick pans are **coated with polytetrafluoroethylene, also known as Teflon.**
 
• 
 Teflon is a polymer of tetrafluoroethylene also known as **polytetrafluoroethylene**.
 
 
• 
 Teflon is a synthetic chemical made up of carbon and fluorine atoms.
 
 
• 
 It was first made in the 1930s and provides a nonreactive, nonstick, and almost frictionless surface 
 
 
• **Teflon coatings are made from a mixture of PFOA and PTFE, the PFOA is not much present in the nonstick coatings as it burns out in the process.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **To reduce the exposure to harmful toxic substances from PTFE, the following can be useful :**

 
 
• Avoid heating up an empty PTFE coated pan because it overheats very quickly releasing fumes harmful to human inhaling.
 
• Temperatures over 260 degrees damage the cookware very fast. Using low heat when cooking will increase the life span of the nonstick pan.
 
• Once the Teflon pan shows scratches, its time you replace it or recoat using a nonstick coating spray.
 
• Always ensure to clean using hands and prevent scratching the nonstick coating.
 
• When cooking is better to use wooden or silicone utensils and avoid scratching, unlike metal utensils.
